clue.text: Ship put about source of epidemic, having limited expertise

indicators.note: the first two pieces hold and hem in the expertise, so they go around it on either side

parts.note: to air a rumour is to put it about
a carrier spreads a disease without necessarily suffering it
craft means skill or know-how

explanation.surface: Someone with only a little know-how has spread the source of an outbreak around a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'source of epidemic' is a whole phrase for a disease spreader, not a first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A naval vessel from which planes take off and land is a kind of ship.

clue.text: A committee with four names arranged to protect university building of historic interest

indicators.note: a protector surrounds what it shields, so the shuffled letters wrap round the university letter
letters that are arranged are put in a new order
four of them means the pair of name letters is doubled to make four in all

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for name; two names give a pair of them

explanation.surface: A committee rearranges four names to save a university building of historic interest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'four names' is four Ns; 'arranged' shuffles them with COMMITTEE into NCIENTMONMENT, and 'to protect' puts U inside, after the opening A.
explanation.definitionFit: A protected old structure or site, such as a castle ruin, is officially listed as one of these.

clue.text: Former worker, weary, having mostly to stagger around

indicators.note: the shortened staggering word goes round the word for weary
most of the word, with its last letter dropped

parts.note: to reel is to stagger
to tire is to grow weary

explanation.surface: A tired former worker is staggering about.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has stopped working for good, on a pension, was formerly a worker.

clue.text: Way to dismiss active staff

indicators.note: dismissing sends a piece away, so this letter is removed from the street word

parts.note: a road is a way

explanation.surface: A way of getting rid of active staff members.
explanation.walkthrough: 'staff' looks like employees, but it is a stick.
explanation.definitionFit: A staff is a long pole or stick, as is a rod.

clue.text: Look into morass over debts associated with crime

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece over another comes first
the word for look goes inside the marsh word

parts.note: a fen is a marsh or morass
lo is an old word meaning look
IOUs are written promises to pay, so debts

explanation.surface: Someone looks into a swamp of debts linked to crime.
explanation.definitionFit: Felonious describes conduct that amounts to a serious criminal offence.

clue.text: One punishes Church accepting a new Rector

indicators.note: the church letters take in the next two pieces between them

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A church takes on a new rector who disciplines people.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who beats people with a cane as a penalty is a punisher.

clue.text: Cherokees rampaging about cowboy finally beginning to dance, getting flushed?

indicators.note: letters on the rampage run wild into a new order
the last letter of the cowboy word
the opening letter of the dance word

explanation.surface: Cherokees run riot around a cowboy and start dancing, red in the face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rampaging' shuffles CHEROKEES with Y and D; 'about' merely joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruddy, glowing cheeks are a flushed look, the question mark marking an example.

clue.text: Clinker, say, that is full of carbon — hint to bring in boron

indicators.note: the abbreviation for that is holds the carbon symbol

parts.note: C is the chemical symbol for carbon

indicators.note: the hint word takes the boron symbol inside it

parts.note: a cue is a hint or prompt
B is the chemical symbol for boron

explanation.surface: Industrial clinker full of carbon, with a hint about adding boron, as in a chemistry lab.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clinker' suggests furnace residue, but it is something that clinks in a glass.
explanation.definitionFit: A frozen cube in a drink clinks against the glass, so it is jokingly a clinker.

clue.text: Author gestures, vaguely encompassing second reference work

indicators.note: the shuffled letters take in the abbreviation for second
something done vaguely is unclear, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: An author gestures vaguely at a second book of reference.
explanation.definitionFit: Peter Mark Roget's book of synonyms is a standard reference.

clue.text: Quote line about a Duke in fortress

indicators.note: the quoting word goes around the other pieces

parts.note: to cite is to quote

explanation.surface: A line is quoted about a duke in his fortress.
explanation.definitionFit: A citadel is a stronghold guarding a city.

clue.text: Recalled information about stone, say, in investments?

indicators.note: the turned word goes around the stone abbreviation and the example word
called back, so the word is read in the other direction

parts.note: gen is slang for information
ST is the abbreviation for stone, the weight
e.g. means for example, so say

explanation.surface: Someone recalls details about a gemstone held in an investment portfolio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stone' is the weight abbreviation, not a gem.
explanation.definitionFit: Money set aside and saved for the future is a store of investments.

clue.text: Not beginning to carry or lug

indicators.note: the word loses its opening letter

parts.note: to bear is to carry

explanation.surface: An instruction on how not to start carrying or lugging something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lug' looks like a verb next to carry, but it is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Lug is slang for the organ of hearing on the side of the head.

clue.text: Sporting venue: ecstatic, we hear, about to try to win

indicators.note: says the word is taken by its sound, not its spelling

parts.note: sent means thrilled, carried away
re means about or concerning
to court is to try to win someone's love

explanation.surface: At a sports venue, a thrilled competitor is trying to win.
explanation.definitionFit: The main show court at Wimbledon, a famous tennis venue.

clue.text: Drink? Caught a second time with ale brewing

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: something brewing is being mixed up, so these letters change order

parts.note: mo is a moment or second

explanation.surface: Someone is caught brewing ale a second time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brewing' shuffles MO, TIME and ALE into AMOMILETE; mo is short for moment.
explanation.definitionFit: An infusion of herb flowers is a soothing beverage.

clue.text: Article's penetrated by minor excited particles

indicators.note: the article piece is entered by the other letters

parts.note: the definite article plus S

indicators.note: excited letters are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: An article is penetrated by excited minor particles, as in physics.
explanation.definitionFit: Thermions are charged particles given off by a hot body.

clue.text: Quiet about this after low rough? Not very

indicators.note: the quiet word goes around the other pieces

parts.note: sh is a call for quiet

indicators.note: this follows the lowing word

parts.note: to low is to moo, like a cow

explanation.surface: A golfer hushes over a quiet shot from low rough, not very rough.
explanation.definitionFit: Fairly even, or a little level, is the reverse of not very rough.

clue.text: Get rid of first person in Paris to come in drunk etc.

indicators.note: the French pronoun enters the shuffled letters
drunk letters reel into a new order

parts.note: je is French for I

explanation.surface: A drunk Parisian who comes in is thrown out, and so on.
explanation.definitionFit: To throw out or expel is to remove.

clue.text: Nothing simple about source of unusual hatred

parts.note: O is zero, nothing

indicators.note: the word for simple goes around the first letter

parts.note: dim means simple or slow-witted

indicators.note: the first letter of unusual

explanation.surface: Nothing simple about the cause of unusual hatred.
explanation.definitionFit: Odium is widespread loathing or disgust.

clue.text: Popular father retaining power to encourage

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular

indicators.note: the father word holds the power letter inside it

parts.note: to sire is to father; a sire is a father

explanation.surface: A popular father with power tries to encourage.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to inspire someone is to fill them with confidence and the urge to act.

clue.text: Keep building to standard?

indicators.note: A to B joins B onto A, so the building word follows the standard word

parts.note: stock means standard, as in a stock answer
a pile is a large building

explanation.surface: Keep building up to a standard?
explanation.walkthrough: 'standard' looks like the definition, but it is wordplay; the definition is 'Keep', used as a noun for a store.
explanation.definitionFit: A reserve of goods put by for later use is a store one holds, a keep.

clue.text: One politician taking on stupid European in stalled debate?

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
MP is a Member of Parliament
an ass is a fool; used loosely for stupid

explanation.surface: A politician takes on a stupid European in a deadlocked debate.
explanation.definitionFit: A deadlock where no progress is possible, as in an argument going nowhere.

clue.text: A lot of cult editions distributed without asking

indicators.note: distributed letters are spread around into a new order
most of the word, with its last letter dropped

explanation.surface: A cult hands out lots of editions to people who never asked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A lot of' cuts CULT to CUL; 'distributed' shuffles CUL EDITIONS.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unrequested comes without anyone asking for it.

clue.text: Men leaving unpleasant tasks succeeded in game

indicators.note: the men letters go out of the chores word

parts.note: chores are tedious tasks
OR is other ranks, ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: With unpleasant tasks left behind, the men succeed at a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Men' are the chessmen in the surface; here they are OR.
explanation.definitionFit: A board game for two with kings, queens and pawns.

clue.text: Vegetable that's almost entirely vegetable matter

indicators.note: all but the last letter of the word

parts.note: peat is decayed plant matter

explanation.surface: A vegetable made almost entirely of plant matter.
explanation.definitionFit: A small green seed eaten as a vegetable.

clue.text: Letter in Latin in ensemble's latest track

indicators.note: the last letter of the ensemble word
the Latin letter goes inside the track word

parts.note: a piste is a ski track

explanation.surface: A letter written in Latin is found in a musical ensemble's latest track.
explanation.definitionFit: An epistle is a formal letter, as in those of the New Testament.

clue.text: I note canine is — with gold — adjacent to this?

definitions.text: I note canine is — with gold — adjacent to this?

parts.note: C stands for canine in dental notation
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A dentist observes that a canine sits next to another tooth.
explanation.walkthrough: Dentists chart teeth as I, C, PM and M, so C is canine.
explanation.definitionFit: The front cutting tooth sits next to the canine in the mouth.

clue.text: Reduced-price salad veg

indicators.note: the price word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: cost means price

explanation.surface: A cut-price salad vegetable.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-leaved lettuce variety, also called romaine, used in salads.

clue.text: Excellent contacts in the radio business

definitions.meaning: fine wires touching the crystal in early crystal radio sets

explanation.surface: Superb contacts in the broadcasting industry.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means superb, and old crystal sets used a fine wire contact with this name.
